// SITE BLOCKS

Section & pattern library 177 blocks

Every pattern has a unique T-number. Tell an AI “use T041” and point it at catalog.json: it maps the ID to an anchor, a set, and the source file it is authored in. The whole library is this one page.

Two switches sit at the top. Theme reskins everything, because no block contains a raw colour: they all read the tokens in assets/base.css. Set filters down to the core library or the e-commerce blocks, and hides the blocks you are not looking at.

Core library 106 blocks

The general-purpose set: foundations, sections, patterns and UI. Every one is token-driven, so the theme switch above reskins the lot.

The blocks

Every block below, in T order. Nothing to click into: scroll, or use a T-number from the list above.

Foundations T001–T003

The token system itself: palette, type and the rules every other block obeys.

Back to the list ↑
T001

Colour palette

Every design token as a live swatch, named, with its role and both theme values, so you can see what a block is allowed to use.

This library is token driven. A block must never hardcode a colour: it names a token, and the active theme decides the value. Every chip below is filled with var(--token), so flipping Theme in the toolbar repaints this page live. The pair under each name is what that token resolves to in each theme, read back from the stylesheet rather than typed in.

Surfaces

Grounds, from the page backdrop up to the cleanest card fill.

--bg-black Page ground Dark#000000 Moonrite#ffffff
--bg Section ground Dark#050505 Moonrite#ffffff
--bg-2 Raised panel, card fill Dark#0a0a0a Moonrite#f6f2ec
--bg-3 Inset well, input fill, code block Dark#0b0d10 Moonrite#ded6c9
--bg-card The cleanest card fill Dark#060606 Moonrite#ffffff
Text

Four steps down. All four clear AA on every surface token above.

--text Headings and strong text Dark#f9fafb Moonrite#000000
--text-2 Body copy Dark#cbd5e1 Moonrite#1d2437
--text-3 Secondary and muted text Dark#9ca3af Moonrite#4a4a4a
--text-4 Meta, captions and placeholders Dark#7b828f Moonrite#565656
Borders

Three weights of line, from a hairline divider to a strong edge.

--border Hairline dividers and guide lines Dark#1f2937 Moonrite#c6cdd8
--border-2 Default visible border Dark#374151 Moonrite#9aa4b8
--border-3 Strong border, circle nodes, number boxes Dark#4b5563 Moonrite#2a344e
Accent

One signature colour per theme. Text on an accent fill always takes --accent-ink, never --text: the accent is bright in one theme and dark in the other, so a fixed ink fails in one of them.

--accent The signature colour: CTAs, eyebrows, active states Dark#ff7f1f Moonrite#2a344e
--accent-hover Hover on an accent fill Dark#e66a15 Moonrite#000000
--accent-deep Pressed or deeper fill Dark#e85d04 Moonrite#1d2437
--accent-light Highlight band, secondary accent fill Dark#ff9d52 Moonrite#e1ac5a
--accent-ink Text that sits on an accent fill Dark#0a0a0a Moonrite#ded6c9
--accent-wash Accent-tinted surface, subtle Dark#1a1206 Moonrite#eceef2
--accent-wash-2 Accent-tinted surface, stronger Dark#3a1e05 Moonrite#c6cdd8
--accent-line Accent at low alpha: rules, glows, focus rings Dark#ff7f1f55 Moonrite#2a344e55
--accent-faint Accent at very low alpha Dark#ff7f1f1f Moonrite#2a344e1f

Meaning, not identity. A status colour on its own wash is the safe pairing, and --status-ink is the ink on a solid status fill.

For charts, tag groups, legends and avatar tints, where the colour carries identity rather than meaning. Never use a status colour here: green on a chart should not read as success.

Commerce and neutral

Colours that must not borrow a status hue. A saving is not an error, a five-star review is not a warning, and an overflow count means nothing at all.

T076

FAQ, expanded by default

The accordion pattern with every item open on load (set the open attribute). Collapse any you don’t need.

Do I have to burn the card?

No. Burning is optional and for adults only. Tearing the card up is an equally complete release, and the better choice if you're unsure or open flames aren't permitted where you are.

What if I miss a month?

Nothing happens. There's no streak to keep. The next full moon comes around either way, and the card will still be in the box.

Do you ship outside Australia?

Not yet. We deliver Australia-wide, and standard delivery is free.

T162

Reading-progress bar

A progress bar pinned to the top of a scroll container that fills as you read inside the box.

Scroll this box to watch the bar fill. The progress is measured against this container’s scroll position, not the window’s.

Most of us are good at deciding things and not so good at closing them out. Intentions pile up in notes apps and on the backs of receipts, half-remembered and never finished.

Moonrite is built around one small move: write the thing down properly, on a card that exists just for it. One card a month, on the full moon, and that’s the whole practice.

Each card carries that month’s full moon over an Australian landmark. January is Byron Bay Lighthouse. By December you’ve crossed the country without leaving the kitchen table.

When you’re ready to let it go, you choose the ending. Burning is the signature ritual, it’s optional, and it’s for adults. If you’d rather not light anything, tear the card up instead. Both count.

There’s no streak to keep and no app to check. Miss a month and the next full moon simply comes around again.

You don’t have to believe anything in particular for this to be worth doing. Writing something down and deciding to be done with it is a very old, very human trick.

That’s the whole idea. Twelve cards, twelve full moons, and a bit of room each month to put something down and leave it there.

Product accordion

What's in the box

Twelve monthly cards, each with the full moon over an Australian landmark on the front and writing space on the back. One card a month, January through December 2027.

Plus a welcome card, a how-to card, a fire safety card that stays in the box, a locations index, a next-year signup card, and a few spares in case a month goes sideways.

The details
Cards
12 monthly, plus supporting cards and spares
Format
Boxed set
Origin
Australian made
Delivery
Australia only
The ritual

On the night of the full moon, write what you're ready to let go of on the back of that month's card. Then release it.

Burning is optional. Adults only. If you're unsure, or open flames aren't permitted where you are, do not light it. Tear the card instead. A torn card is a complete release.

Delivery and returns

Standard delivery is free Australia wide. Express is $16.95. We post from Maroochydore, Queensland, and email you when your box is on its way.

If your deck arrives damaged, get in touch and we'll sort it out. Nothing here limits your rights under Australian Consumer Law.

Prettier in person than on the site

Ordered the week it launched. The illustrations are proper vintage travel poster stuff, deep navy with gold line-work, and the box is sturdier than it needed to be. We could not wait for January, so we used one of the spare cards at the August full moon. Ten quiet minutes at the kitchen table, and that was that.

NH Nadia H. Verified buyer · Fremantle, WA 2 Aug 2026
★★★★★ ★★★★★

Use a ballpoint, not a fine-liner

The cards are lovely and January's lighthouse is the standout. One mark against: the writable side has a slight coating, so a fine-liner smudges if you are impatient. A ballpoint is perfect. Posted to Freo in four days with the free delivery, and the box arrived without a dent.

    Behind the deck

    Twelve landmarks, one moon

    Every card in the 2027 deck sets the full moon over a different Australian landmark, from Byron Bay Lighthouse in January to the Twelve Apostles in December. Amy drew them the way old travel posters were drawn, deep navy skies and warm gold line-work, on the theory that a card you might burn should be beautiful first.

      Password reset

      Both halves of the reset: the request form with its check-your-email state, and the set-new-password form with a strength meter and a live match check.

      Step 1: request a link

      Enter the email on your account and we will send a link that stays valid for 60 minutes.

      Check your email

      If an account uses that address, a reset link is on its way. It expires in 60 minutes, and it can only be used once.

      Nothing arrived? Look in spam, then try again in a couple of minutes.

      Step 2: set a new password

      Start typing to see how strong it is.

      Password updated. You are signed in on this device only.

      Use eight characters or more, mixing letters, numbers and a symbol. A passphrase of three unrelated words works well.
